[A reading journey for hands-on practitioners]{.eyebrow}

# Touch is not one sense

::: {.stand}
Skin carries at least two separate systems, and they are not sending the same
message. One tells you *what* you are touching. The other answers mainly to being
touched *affectionately* — found by accident, confirmed by a man who had lost the
ordinary sense of touch, and it fires hardest at one particular speed.
What follows is what we found reading our way through it: what each system responds to,
what touch does to pain and to relationships, and which of the popular claims we could
not get to stand up.
:::
::::

:::: {.about}

::: {.ab}
[What this is]{.k}

A plain-language walk through the research on touch — the
[sense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somatosensory_system){.wiki}, not the technique.
Twelve short stops, about thirty minutes, with figures you can operate rather than only
look at.
:::

::: {.ab}
[Who it is for]{.k}

Anyone whose work involves putting hands on other people: massage therapists,
bodyworkers, physiotherapists, osteopaths, nurses, midwives, somatic and trauma
practitioners. **No science background is assumed** — we did not begin with much
of one either.
:::

::: {.ab}
[How it is sourced]{.k}

Every claim here points to a named paper, cited at the top of its section and listed at
the foot of the page it appears on — so you can go and check where we have read it wrong.
Where researchers disagree, and here they disagree a good deal, we have tried to say so
rather than pick a side. It is not medical advice and not a technique manual.
:::

::::

## The four parts {#parts}

The journey runs in order, and each part builds on the one before it. Every page
carries its own references at the foot.

::: {.reading}
[**One · the territory**](territory.qmd){.n} — two roads, the receptors they arrive on,
and how finely skin can actually resolve what it feels.

[**Two · the second system**](second-system.qmd){.n} — how the slow road was found, the
patient who proved it carries an experience, and the two things it is tuned to.

[**Three · what touch does**](what-touch-does.qmd){.n} — pain, the map of who may touch
you where, and an honest sorting of how sure anyone can be about any of it.

[**Four · being honest about it**](being-honest.qmd){.n} — four things the field has had
to take back, and why the fibre is not the feeling.

[**What we carry back into the room**](carry-back.qmd){.n} — ten things we came away
with, further reading, and the complete reference list.
:::

::: {.foot}
Assembled in 2026 from the literature as it stood. A reading of published research,
written for people who work with touch. It is not medical advice, it does not describe a
technique, and it cannot tell you what the person in front of you wants.
:::
